nodes.label: Bilateral periorbital purpura present for five years
Patient is a 68-year-old man from Brazil with a known family history of cardiac condition in a sibling (deceased at age 65)

Medical history includes medically treated endocarditis with nonrheumatic mitral valve insufficiency seven years prior, prostate cancer treated with transurethral resection, and right-hand carpal tunnel syndrome with surgical release
Physical examination confirmed bilateral periorbital purpura and the patient denied any history of trauma to the area
Serum free light chain ratio is elevated but immunofixation shows no monoclonal protein
Echocardiography shows left ventricular wall thickening, restrictive filling, and apical sparing with reduced strain
Nuclear scintigraphy shows grade 3 cardiac uptake
Genetic testing reveals pathogenic TTR Ala19Asp heterozygous variant
Periorbital purpura is caused by amyloid infiltration of dermal vessels
